newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Oct 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - Oct 20.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TIMES
-- PEARSON SHAKE-UP COLD LEAD TO SALE OF TV ARM

According to city analysts, Pearson are set to hive off its television interests either by joint venture or sale. New chairman, Dennis Stevenson and new chief executive Marjorie Scardino are both supporters of a smaller more focused range of activities, although they are unlikely to make any quick decisions on the group's direction.
-- SEARS WILL SELL ELECTRICITY BY MAIL-ORDER CATALOGUE

Sears is in talks with a number of electricity companies to sell cut price electricity to its shoppers by its Freemans, mail order catalogue. Sears could either partner an electricity generator that would sell it power at a wholesale price or it would team up with a Regional electricity company.
-- SUNDERLAND TO JOIN FOOTBALL CLUB FLOATS

Sunderland Football Club is set to join the increasing number of teams quoted on the Stock Exchange when it goes public at the end of this year. Charterhouse Tileny and NM Rothschild have been appointed to advise the club on the flotation that could value it at around 30 million pounds stg.
-- QUALITY BOOSTS EXPORTS, SAYS TREASURY STUDY

According to academic research commissioned by the Treasury, British industry is winning a higher share of world trade because of improve quality and the impact of inward investment, and not from falls in the pound. The research suggests that the government should not be unduly concerned about sterling's recent rise.
-- GREYCOAT FACES BREAK-UP CALL

UK Active Value, the second largest investor in Greycoat, will tomorrow call for the property company to break up its 500 million pounds stg portfolio. The investor, with an 11 per cent stake in the company is to call for a shareholders meeting so it can put its proposal to a vote. It hopes Greycoat will offer its assets for sale over the next 18 months and return the cash to investors.
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- BT IN TALKS TO BUILD 5 BILLION POUNDS SUPERHIGHWAY

BT has plans to transform Britain's telephone network into the most technologically advanced in the world, with a 5 billion pounds stg investment. The plans involve fitting a revolutionary system enhancer to all its 22.5 million phone lines which would allow them to carry high-quality television pictures an high-speed computer data. The plans are expected to be met with fierce opposition from Oftel, the telecoms watchdog.
-- BARCLAYS SELLS GLOBAL CUSTODY TO MORGAN

Barclays Bank and in talks with Morgan Stanley, the US investment bank, to sell its global custody business. Barclays has decided that the custody business, which handles 200 billion pounds stg, with its wafer-thin margins, high compliance costs and technology costs, is not a core business.
-- WEDGWOOD TARGETS RIVAL ROSENTHAL

Waterford Wedgwood, the crystal and bone china group, looks set to enter takeover talks with Rosenthal, the German china and porcelain business. Waterford Wedgwood's chairman, Tony O'Reilly who saved the company from near bankruptcy six years ago, is now ready to propose himself as saviour of the beleaguered German company.
-- HORLICK TO REVIVE MG UNIT TRUST ARM

Morgan Grenfell Assett Management's new chief executive Robert Smith has asked Nicola Horlick, the star fund manager, to work in the group's unit trust business. Horlick, who has just returned from maternity leave, will play a key role in turning the unit trust business round in the wake of the Peter Young scandal.
-- EUROTUNNEL AXES JOBS IN SEARCH FOR 20 MILLION POUNDS SAVINGS

In an attempt to make savings of 20 million pounds stg a year, Eurotunnel is set to cut more than 650 jobs from its 3,500 strong workforce. It is believed that many of the employees are on contracts which will ensure the lowest possible one-off redundancy charge. INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- EMU FORCED ON PENSION FUNDS

Germany's finance minister is understood to have approved in principle the conversion of all existing German government debt from marks to euros when the single currency is introduced in 1999. It emerged last week that Germany is prepared to convert its entire bond market into euros at the first stage of monetary union rather than at the end of the transition period in 2002. Analysts in the UK believe the implications of such a change are huge and that pension funds with large holdings in government debt will be trading largely n euros, and certainly speed up the wide use of the euro in all market transactions.
-- BERLUSCONI VERDICT DUE

The London High Court look set to decide this week whether to snub the Home Secretary and refuse to agree to the release of secret documents that reveal a secret offshore empire set up by the former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi.
-- BELL WIN TO SPUR CABLE SHAKE-UP
Bell Cablemedia is near to victory in the long-running fight for control of the UK cable TV company, Videotron. The 600
million pounds stg acquisition of Videotron, would push Bell Cablemedia up alongside TeleWest as the country's largest cable operators and confirm its commitment to the UK market.
-- VIRGIN BIDS TO PUT 'NON-NERDS' ONLINE

Virgin's Internet service to be launched next month as part of a joint venture with International Cabletel the US cable firm, will be offered free to its subscribers for the first three months as part of an attempt to lure users who have so far shunned the offer of online communication. They believe that someone needs to explain why the Internet is worthwhile and that they are in a good position to do so.
-- GROWTH HIT BY FAILURE OF PRIVATE INITIATIVE

Economic growth has been reduced by up to 0.4 of a percentage point due to the failure of the Government's Private Finance Initiative to make up for a 17 per cent fall in public-sector investment in the first half of the year. Private investors havecovered only a small part of the 1.2 billion pounds stg shortfall.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- GUMMER TAX THREAT TO QUARRY FIRMS

An environmental tax is planned by the government for the 3 billion pounds stg a year gravel industry. John Gummer, the Environment secretary, has told waste industry bosses that he wants to discourage the quarrying of aggregates such as sand, gravel and clay used by the building industry. Experts believe that Mr Gummer's hints at a tax on aggregates, would be introduced as 1 pound stg per ton, which would raise over 200 million pounds a year.
-- FALKLANDS SNUB FOR BRITISH GAS OIL BID

An application by British Gas GAS to explore for oil in the seas around the Falklands oil has been turned down. The decision to be announced on October 28 will be a blow to British Gas who are expected to be one of the few companies to be turned down. The area is of one of the world's last undeveloped territories to be opened to the oil business and could contain around 3 billion barrels of oil worth around 5 billion pounds stg.
-- FORTE SET FOR A RETURN NORTH OF THE BORDER

Rocco Forte is believed to be in negotiations for a series of management contracts, including one for a five star hotel in Glasgow. Forte is said to have signed a confidentiality agreement covering discussions over the hotel and luxury redevelopment of the former Glasgow Sheriff Court.
-- EC TAX SHAKE-UP THREAT TO BRITAIN

A European Commission scheme to harmonise tax rate in member states, especially on savings and to change the way VAT is paid on goods bought in the EU, could have a dramatic impact on Britain where low taxation makes it one of the most attractive countries in the EU for foreign investment and private savings.
-- BLOW FOR THE NORTH AS BROKERS FACE TURMOIL

The stockbroking community in Manchester is in a state of turmoil as Henry Cooke Lumsden, John Siddall and Pilling & Co have all been hit by internal crises. Doubts have been raised about the city's ability to compete with other regional financial centres.
OBSERVER
-- STAKIS CASH CALL TO RAISE 230 MILLION POUNDS
The Glasgow based leisure group,

Stakis, is on the verge of asking shareholders for 230 million pounds stg to buy the Metropole hotel chain from Lonrho. David Michels, the chief executive, is expected to announce the rights issue on Friday, with the deal meaning that investors will be asked to buy one share for every two they already own. The hotel chain is expected to cost over 300 million pounds stg. -- YOUNG 'DIVERTED MONEY FOR HIS OWN BENEFIT' Peter Young the sacked fund manager of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, his ex-employers, has been directly accused of fraud and diverting money for his own benefit. The accusation centres around a Luxembourg 'brass plate' company which wa used as a device for Young to divert money and opportunities for himself. -- DEALERSHIP PLANS PUT 50,000 CAR JOBS AT RISK A sales shake up by Britain's leading motor manufacturers could cost over 50,000 car dealers and mechanics their jobs say industry leaders. Plans by Ford, Vauxhall, Rover and Nissan to reduce the number of franchised dealers over the next five years are supported by research carried out by car retail chain Lex. -- US HEALTH FOOD RETAILER JOINS RACE TO BUY HOLLAND & BARRETT General Nutrition Companies, the Amercian health food retailer is expected to compete with venture capitalists to buy Holland & Barrett, its UK counterpart. The British chain is thought likely to be sold off by the winner of a takeover battle for Lloyds Chemist, its parent company. -- WINDFALL TAX? WE CAN TAKE IT Senior directors at South West Water have confirmed that the company can afford a 100 million pounds stg windfall tax and still manage to reward shareholders well. The company is facing hostile bids from Severn Trent and Wessex Water, has said that it will be able to grow its dividend by 8 per cent above inflation even with the windfall tax. __
MAIL ON SUNDAY
